newsitem.title: UK: ASDA shares edge higher after results.
newsitem.headline: ASDA shares edge higher after results.

text.p: Shares in ASDA Group Plc edged higher in early trading on Thursday after the supermarket operator posted a 15.8 percent rise in first-half profits, at the top end of analysts' expectations.
"It is a very strong performance, they are very strong figures, though not totally unexpected," said Bill Curry, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney.

The stock was up 1/4p at 124 by 0809 GMT in volume of 845,000 shares. ASDA said it had outperformed rivals in the past six months, with same-store sales up 10.2 percent. It said it had exceeded the industry average for 55 straight months.
Curry said ASDA's results suggested that the price war that has gripped the UK food retail sector in recent years was past.

"They are an indicator that the price war in the food retail sector is well and truly over," he said. "I think pricing in the the sector is fairly benign. I think they are an indicator that the sector could surprise some people."
Among other food retailers, Safeway Plc was up 6-1/2p at 397 by 0818 GMT but J Sainsbury Plc dipped 1/2p to 368 and Tesco Plc was unchanged at 353.
ASDA said pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits rose to 160.1 million stg in the first half, at the top end of the range of analysts' expectations.
Profit forecasts had been in a range between 155 million stg and 161 million and the dividend, raised to 0.81p from 0.72p, had been expected to be between 0.8p and 0.9p.
